<div align="center">
    <h1>
        Zabbix FreeIPA Client Template
    </h1>
    <h4>

    <br>

<!-- *********************************************************************************************************************************** -->
<!-- *** BODY ************************************************************************************************************************** -->
<!-- *********************************************************************************************************************************** -->
## Description
This template is designed for FreeIPA clients and focuses on native Zabbix keys wherever possible.
Zabbix Agent 2 **7.0+** is required. DNS response time and SRV checks use agent keys
`net.dns.perf` and `net.dns.record` (executed on the agent, not simple checks). Leaving the DNS
server parameter empty uses the local resolver. Resolver validation parses `/etc/resolv.conf` on
the client.
Exec-based checks are limited to FreeIPA-specific verification (Kerberos keytab test) and
timedatectl status for time sync. The goal is to provide comprehensive visibility into client
health and prevent silent outages (SSSD, DNS, time, packages).

## Monitoring scope
- Package inventory and version tracking (ipa-client, sssd, krb5, oddjob-mkhomedir)
- Service health (sssd, chronyd or systemd-timesyncd)
- Time sync status from timedatectl (NTP service enabled, clock synchronized, timezone)
- DNS resolver settings and validation of `/etc/resolv.conf` (expected IPA DNS like ipa01/ipa02)
- DNS response time (net.dns.perf to IPA DNS servers)
- DNS SRV checks for _kerberos and _ldap (net.dns.record) + per-DNS-server SRV response time/consistency
- Per-DNS-server A record check and response time for `{$IPA.DNS.TEST.NAME}` + consistency vs local resolver
- SSH login + home availability check (requires SSH agent check on Zabbix server/proxy)
- SRV target discovery (from _ldap._tcp), TCP connectivity checks, and DNS response time
- Kerberos keytab test (kinit -k)
- Certificate expiry checks
- SSSD log error patterns (requires active checks; consider narrowing regex or disabling on large fleets)

## Requirements
- **Zabbix 7.0 or higher**
- Zabbix **Agent 2 7.0+** installed on the IPA client (required)
- IPA client components installed (sssd, krb5, ipa-client)
- OpenSSL binary available on the client for CA expiration check
- Zabbix server/proxy must be able to reach the client over SSH for the SSH login check
- Optional extra SSH test requires a dedicated SSH account to verify login and home directory availability
- The SSH test expects a marker file `~/.ZABBIX` in the tested user's home (create it once; with mounted homes this is a one‑time setup)
- timedatectl available on the client (systemd-based systems)
- Active checks enabled if you use the SSSD log monitoring item (`logrt`)
- Optional sudo rule or ACL for the Kerberos keytab test

## Setup
### 1. Install IPA client packages
Install the IPA client and its dependencies using your distribution package manager.
Common packages include `ipa-client`, `sssd`, `krb5`/`krb5-workstation`, and `oddjob-mkhomedir`.

### 2. Download the agent config
```bash
sudo wget https://git.initmax.cz/initMAX-Public/zabbix-templates/-/raw/production/free/FreeIPA_Client/7.0/freeipa_client.conf -O /etc/zabbix/zabbix_agent2.d/freeipa_client.conf
sudo chown zabbix:zabbix /etc/zabbix/zabbix_agent2.d/freeipa_client.conf
```

### 3. Allow Kerberos keytab access (required for the keytab test)
The keytab test uses `sudo` for `kinit`/`kdestroy` by default. Grant sudo rights as below.
If you prefer ACLs instead, remove `sudo` from the user parameter and grant read access to `/etc/krb5.keytab`.
```bash
cat <<'EOF' | sudo tee /etc/sudoers.d/zabbix-ipa-client >/dev/null
Defaults:zabbix !requiretty
zabbix ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/kinit -k -t /etc/krb5.keytab *
zabbix ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/kdestroy
EOF
sudo chmod 440 /etc/sudoers.d/zabbix-ipa-client
sudo visudo -cf /etc/sudoers.d/zabbix-ipa-client
```

### 4. Allow SSSD log access (optional)
If you want the `logrt` item to work, the `zabbix` user must be able to read `/var/log/sssd`.
The file mask uses a regex that matches only `.log` files (`^sssd_.*\.log$`) to avoid `.gz`.
Use ACLs to grant access and persist it for log rotation (default ACLs apply to directories only):
```bash
sudo setfacl -m u:zabbix:rx /var/log/sssd
sudo setfacl -m u:zabbix:r /var/log/sssd/sssd_*.log
sudo setfacl -d -m u:zabbix:rx /var/log/sssd
```

### 5. Restart agent
```bash
sudo systemctl restart zabbix-agent2
```

### 6. Test items
```bash
sudo -u zabbix zabbix_agent2 -t systemd.unit.get[sssd.service]
sudo -u zabbix zabbix_agent2 -t vfs.file.contents[/etc/resolv.conf]
sudo -u zabbix zabbix_agent2 -t net.dns.perf[,ipa01.example.com,A]
sudo -u zabbix zabbix_agent2 -t net.dns.record[,_kerberos._tcp.example.com,SRV]
sudo -u zabbix zabbix_agent2 -t ipa.kerberos.kinit[EXAMPLE.COM]
sudo -u zabbix zabbix_agent2 -t ipa.time.timedatectl
sudo -u zabbix zabbix_agent2 -t ipa.ca.notafter
```

### 6. Import template
Import [`template_freeipa_client_7.0.yaml`](./7.0/template_freeipa_client_7.0.yaml) and link it to the IPA client host.

Optionally tune macro thresholds (see below).

### Mandatory macros
The following macros must be set:
- `{$IPA.DNS.SERVERS.MATCH}`
- `{$IPA.DNS.SEARCH.MATCH}`
- `{$IPA.DNS.SRV.DOMAIN}`
- `{$IPA.DNS.TEST.NAME}`
- `{$IPA.PKG.VERSION.MATCH}`
- `{$IPA.KINIT.REALM}`
- `{$IPA.SSH.USER}`
- `{$IPA.SSH.PASS}`

### Macros used
| Macro | Description | Default |
|-------|-------------|---------|
| `{$IPA.DNS.SERVERS.MATCH}` | **MANDATORY.** Regex of expected DNS servers from `nameserver` lines in `/etc/resolv.conf` (full match; use IPs like `IP_DNS_IPA1\|IP_DNS_IPA2`) | `IP_DNS_IPA1\|IP_DNS_IPA2` |
| `{$IPA.DNS.SEARCH.MATCH}` | **MANDATORY.** Regex of expected search/domain from `/etc/resolv.conf` (what your clients should search) | `example.com` |
| `{$IPA.DNS.SRV.DOMAIN}` | **MANDATORY.** Domain suffix used for SRV lookups, e.g. `_kerberos._tcp.<domain>` and `_ldap._tcp.<domain>`; typically your IPA realm domain like `lin.example.com` | `example.com` |
| `{$IPA.DNS.RESP.TIME.WARN}` | Warning threshold for DNS response time (seconds) | `0.2s` |
| `{$IPA.DNS.RESP.TIME.CRIT}` | Critical threshold for DNS response time (seconds) | `0.5s` |
| `{$IPA.DNS.TEST.NAME}` | **MANDATORY.** FQDN queried by `net.dns.perf` (should be resolvable via IPA DNS) | `ipa01.example.com` |
| `{$IPA.DNS.NODATA.WINDOW}` | Time window for DNS nodata triggers | `15m` |
| `{$IPA.PACKAGES.MATCH}` | Regex for package discovery filter (what should be tracked) | `ipa-client\|sssd\|krb5\|oddjob-mkhomedir` |
| `{$IPA.PKG.VERSION.MATCH}` | **MANDATORY.** Regex of approved package versions (applies to all discovered packages). Trigger requires a non-empty value. Example: `2.11.1-2.0.1.el10_1.1\|0.34.7-14.el10\|1.21.3-8.0.1.el10_0\|4.12.2-24.0.1.el10_1.1` | `version1\|version2` |
| `{$IPA.SSSD.LOG.ERROR}` | Regex of error patterns in SSSD logs (matches are reported by `logrt`) | `ERROR\|Offline\|Failed` |
| `{$IPA.SSSD.LOG.WINDOW}` | Time window for log error trigger evaluation | `5m` |
| `{$IPA.CERT.EXPIRE.WARN}` | Warning threshold for IPA CA cert expiry (time left) | `7d` |
| `{$IPA.KINIT.REALM}` | **MANDATORY.** Kerberos realm appended as `@REALM` for keytab test | `EXAMPLE.COM` |
| `{$IPA.TIMEZONE.MATCH}` | Regex of expected timezone from timedatectl (leave empty to disable timezone check) | `Europe/Prague` |
| `{$IPA.SSH.USER}` | **MANDATORY.** SSH username for login test | (empty) |
| `{$IPA.SSH.PASS}` | **MANDATORY.** SSH password for login test | (empty) |
| `{$IPA.SSH.HOME.FILE}` | Marker file in user home directory to verify home availability | `.ZABBIX` |
| `{$IPA.SSH.NODATA.WINDOW}` | Time window for SSH nodata trigger | `20m` |
